title: Retrieval Beyond Documents
subtitle: Capability Retrieval for Language Agents
description: Retrieval Beyond Documents (RBD), a NAACL 2027 workshop on capability retrieval for language agents. Overview, call for papers, speakers, program, and organizers.

topics.title: Representation & indexing
topics.description: Represent tools, APIs, skills, workflows, memories, models, and agents through language, schemas, code, demonstrations, traces, graphs, and embeddings.

topics.title: Retrieval, routing & composition
topics.description: Retrieve and route across capability types, accounting for dependencies, compatibility, permissions, reliability, and cost. Compose the right set for the task.

topics.title: Retrieval in the agent loop
topics.description: Condition retrieval on execution state, plans, and observations. Study reformulation, clarification, decomposition, invocation, delegation, replanning, recovery, and abstention.

topics.title: Action grounded evaluation
topics.description: Evaluate retrieval, incorporation, invocation, composition, and execution. Develop complete set and dependency aware metrics, calibration, and resource constrained evaluation.

topics.title: Ecosystems & deployment
topics.description: Build dynamic, federated, and access controlled registries. Explore Model Context Protocol ecosystems, provenance, permissions, freshness, observability, caching, and reliability.

speakers.name: Iryna Gurevych
speakers.bio: Iryna Gurevych is a Professor of Computer Science at TU Darmstadt and heads the Ubiquitous Knowledge Processing Lab. Her research connects semantic representations, information retrieval, and the reliability of language models. She co-authored Sentence-BERT, which makes semantic similarity search practical through reusable sentence embeddings, and BEIR, a benchmark for testing retrieval systems across diverse tasks and domains. Her broader work spans generative AI, AI safety, and AI for science, including the InterText project on relationships across documents. She is an ACL Fellow and a past ACL President, and received the Royal Society’s Milner Award and Lecture in 2025.

speakers.name: Graham Neubig
speakers.bio: Graham Neubig is an Associate Professor at Carnegie Mellon University’s Language Technologies Institute, where he leads NeuLab, and Chief Scientist at OpenHands. His research spans language models, code generation, multilingual NLP, and agents that learn from experience. He co-authored OpenHands, an open platform for agents that write code, use the command line, and browse the web. His work on Agent Workflow Memory studies how agents can extract reusable workflows from past tasks and apply them to new problems. His later work on the OpenHands Software Agent SDK focuses on composable tools, memory, and sandboxed execution. He also develops open research software and freely available NLP teaching materials.

speakers.name: Scott Wen-tau Yih
speakers.bio: Scott Wen-tau Yih is a Research Scientist at Meta Fundamental AI Research, working on neural retrieval and language models grounded in external knowledge. He co-authored Dense Passage Retrieval, which learns representations of questions and passages for open domain question answering, and the original RAG paper, which combines neural retrieval with text generation. His recent work on Reasoning Memory retrieves reusable procedural knowledge from earlier reasoning trajectories to guide new problems in mathematics, science, and coding. Previously, he held research positions at the Allen Institute for AI and Microsoft Research. He is an ACL Fellow and served as a program co-chair of EMNLP 2021.

speakers.name: Jimmy Lin
speakers.bio: Jimmy Lin is a Professor and holds the David R. Cheriton Chair in the School of Computer Science at the University of Waterloo. His research brings together information retrieval, natural language processing, and data management, with a strong emphasis on reproducible systems. His work includes Pyserini, a toolkit for sparse, dense, and hybrid retrieval, and RankZephyr, an open language model for reranking search results. More recently, he co-authored AgentIR, which uses an agent’s reasoning trace alongside its query to improve retrieval during deep research. He is an ACM Fellow, an ACL Fellow, and a member of the SIGIR Academy.

organizers.name: Hitesh Laxmichand Patel
organizers.bio: Hitesh Laxmichand Patel is a Principal Applied Scientist and Tech Lead at Oracle, where he leads research on agentic and knowledge grounded AI systems. His work spans agentic orchestration, Agentic RAG, tool retrieval, and skill discovery. He has organized workshops, serves in senior reviewing and Area Chair roles, and mentors emerging researchers.

organizers.name: Akari Asai
organizers.bio: Akari Asai is an Assistant Professor at Carnegie Mellon University and a Research Scientist at the Allen Institute for AI. Her research spans retrieval augmented and modular language models, adaptive retrieval, tools, and deep research agents, including recent reasoning aware retrieval work (Chen et al., 2026). She has organized workshops, tutorials, shared tasks, and competitions across major NLP/ML venues.

organizers.name: Omar Khattab
organizers.bio: Omar Khattab is an Assistant Professor and the TIBCO Founders’ Career Development Professor in MIT EECS. His research develops neural retrieval and reliable compositional language model systems. Recent work includes OBLIQ-Bench on latent and implicit retrieval needs (Tchuindjo et al., 2026). He has co-organized workshops on compound AI systems and late interaction retrieval.

organizers.name: Danqi Chen
organizers.bio: Danqi Chen is an Associate Professor of Computer Science at Princeton University, co-leads the Princeton NLP Group, and is an Associate Director of Princeton Language and Intelligence. Her research spans text understanding, knowledge representation, retrieval, reasoning, and QA. Recent work includes BRIGHT (Su et al., 2025) and long horizon agentic search (Yen et al., 2025). She received her Ph.D. from Stanford in 2018.

organizers.name: Zifei Wang
organizers.bio: Zifei Wang is affiliated with the IMA Product Center at Tencent. His research focuses on multimodal information retrieval, ranking, and routing for Large Language Model agents. His recent work covers areas such as skill retrieval and capabilities (Wang et al., 2026), as well as multimodal image and text retrieval.

organizers.name: Avi Sil
organizers.bio: Avi Sil is Senior Director of Applied Science at Oracle, where he leads teams developing AI agent technologies. His research spans RAG, agentic workflows, inference time methods, verification, and natural language to code systems. He has served the ACL community as area chair, track chair, and demonstration chair.

organizers.name: Sewon Min
organizers.bio: Sewon Min is an Assistant Professor in EECS at UC Berkeley and a Research Scientist at the Allen Institute for AI. Her research focuses on understanding and advancing large language models, including their adaptability, factuality, reasoning, and use of large text corpora. She has organized workshops and tutorials on retrieval based language models and foundation models.

organizers.name: Connor Shorten
organizers.bio: Connor Shorten is a Research Scientist at Weaviate. His research focuses on the intersection of AI and Database Systems. His most recent work on IRPAPERS compares text and image based retrieval and question answering systems.
